Fit a concentration-response model separately at each level of a factor

Source: R/bnec_group.R
bnec_group.Rd

Fits the model set independently within each level of a grouping factor, model-averaging within each level, and returns a bayesnecgroupfit. Crossed model weights across levels are then available from the per-level weights alone.

bnec_group(formula, data, group_var, family = NULL, ...)

Arguments

formula

A bayesnecformula, as passed to bnec.

data

A data.frame containing the data.

group_var

A character string naming the column of data that carries the factor.

family

A family function, string, or NULL. If NULL it is chosen once from the whole response and passed down — see Details.

...

Further arguments passed to bnec for every level.

Value

An object of class bayesnecgroupfit.

Details

Why the levels can be fitted separately

Factor levels partition the data disjointly and share no parameters, so the log likelihood is a sum over levels and the expected log predictive density is additive. Under pseudo-BMA — the package default — the crossed model weights are then exactly the outer product of the per-level weight vectors, which is the same identity crossed_weights rests on for the two blocks of a hurdle fit. See crossed_group_weights.

The family is chosen once

The family chosen from each subset separately could differ between levels, which would make the levels incomparable — their elpd contributions would not be on the same scale and the crossed weights would be meaningless. So it is chosen from the whole response and passed down.

Dispersion is per level, deliberately

Separate fits give each level its own sigma/shape/phi. That is a feature, not an oversight: a shared dispersion parameter would break the factorisation the crossed weights depend on. A model with structure spanning levels — shared dispersion, a group-level effect crossing levels, an explicit contrast — is a different model, and is not what this function fits.

What this does not do

It does not refit the favoured combination jointly. That is stage 2 of #33 and lands in the post-processing that the toxval migration moves, so it is deliberately out of scope here.

See also

bnec, crossed_group_weights, bayesnecgroupfit

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(bayesnec)
data(nec_data)
nec_data$site <- rep(c("a", "b"), length.out = nrow(nec_data))
fit <- bnec_group(y ~ crf(x, "nec3param"), data = nec_data,
                  group_var = "site")
nec(fit)
crossed_group_weights(fit)
} # }
